question: What will be the percentage change in the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) (^VIX on Yahoo Finance) from the close on 2026-08-06 to the close on 2026-08-17?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to 100 x (close on 2026-08-17 / close on 2026-08-06 - 1), using daily closes of ^VIX on Yahoo Finance. If there is no close on 2026-08-17, the last close before it is used.
research:
I could not reach Yahoo Finance directly, so the starting value below comes from a secondary source. Most of what I found was published after Aug 7 and I left it out.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question settles on Yahoo Finance ^VIX daily closes: 100 x (Aug 17 close / Aug 6 close - 1). My requests to [Yahoo history](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EVIX/history/) and to FRED's VIXCLS file were refused by the proxy, so I could not check Yahoo's own figure.
- 2026-08-06: VIX closed at **15.15**, down 4.17% from 15.81 on Aug 5, according to [YCharts](https://ycharts.com/indicators/vix_volatility_index). Earlier closes: Aug 4 at 16.50, Aug 3 at 15.86. This is a secondary source but is normally the same Cboe close Yahoo shows.
- The window runs 7 trading days: Aug 7, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 and 17. Aug 17 is a Monday and a normal trading day.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The starting value is fixed (about 15.15), and the outcome depends on the next 7 sessions.
- At about 15, the VIX sits in the low part of its historical range.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-07: The July jobs report was due at 8:30 ET, before forecasts close at 18:00 UTC. One headline says employers unexpectedly cut 23,000 jobs, against expected gains of about 80,000, and that stock futures jumped on it ([Barchart](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3711621/us-stock-futures-jump-as-employers-unexpectedly-cut-23-000-jobs), [CTV](https://www.ctvnews.ca/business/article/us-stock-futures-jump-as-employers-unexpectedly-cut-23000-jobs/)). I could not open these pages, so the figure is unconfirmed.
- 2026-08-03 to 08-06: VIX moved in a 15.15 to 16.50 range and fell into Aug 6 ([YCharts](https://ycharts.com/indicators/vix_volatility_index)).
- About 2026-08-01/02: A Reuters-sourced week-ahead piece described a "teetering" stock market. It said the Fed held rates with three of 12 policymakers dissenting in favor of a hike, Microsoft had its biggest one-day gain since 2008, and Meta fell. It also said nearly 90% of S&P 500 companies had reported, and named the ongoing US war with Iran as a market concern ([Khaleej Times](https://www.khaleejtimes.com/business/markets/wall-st-week-ahead-teetering-us-stock-market-faces-jobs-report-big-earnings-week-3)).
- Background: An undated page says the July FOMC held at 3.50%-3.75% on a 9-3 vote with hawkish dissents ([claritx](https://www.claritx.ai/blog/market-volatility-july-2026-cpi-fed-rates)). It is weakly sourced.

## 4. Base rates
- I did not get a full daily series, so the points below are general patterns of the VIX, not figures I computed for 2026.
  - Over about 7 trading days, the VIX's percentage change typically has a standard deviation of roughly 12-18%.
  - The median change is slightly negative, because volatility tends to drift down in calm markets.
  - The distribution is skewed upward: rises of 20% or more happen on shocks, while falls are usually limited to about 10-20%.
  - When the VIX starts near 15, the room to fall is limited: a level of 12-13 would be roughly -15% to -20%.
- Mid-August seasonality: volatility is often low in summer, but August has produced spikes (2015, 2019, 2024).
- Extra context: VIX options and futures expire on Wednesday, Aug 19, after the window closes.
- The front futures contract is the Aug 2026 VIX future ([Barchart VIQ26](https://www.barchart.com/futures/quotes/VI*0)). I could not get a price for it dated before Aug 7.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on the VIX level or change for this window. Kalshi markets on August CPI exist but are not directly relevant.
- I found no dated expert VIX forecast for mid-August 2026.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-08-07: The market's reaction to the jobs report will set the first day's change.
- About 2026-08-12 or 08-13: The July CPI release, with PPI around the same time. The usual mid-month timing fits: the June CPI came out on July 14 ([BLS schedule](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/2026/home.htm)). I could not confirm the exact date. One preview cites headline CPI expected to ease to 3.8% from 4.2% ([VT Markets](https://www.vtmarkets.com/en-latam/week_ahead/week-ahead-markets-eye-iran-risk-ahead-of-us-cpi/)), but its date is unclear and the figures are unconfirmed.
- Mid-August: Retail sales and other data, probably around Aug 14 (not confirmed).
- Ongoing: US-Iran war headlines and oil price swings are the main geopolitical risk for a jump in volatility. Fed officials' comments on possible hikes also matter.
- Late earnings: NVIDIA usually reports later in August, likely after Aug 17.
- Weekend gap: the Aug 17 Monday close includes any weekend news.
